shower noun

in the bathroom

also take a shower, shower door

modern

Traupman 124: cubiculum balneō pluviō īnstrūctum

balneum pluvium

Other words

  • balneolum pluvium

    also used · modern · Traupman 124

Examples

  • balneolō pluviō ūtor

    I take a showerTraupman 124

  • In cubiculō, quod balneō pluviō īnstrūctum erat, duo lectī et fenestra ūna erant.

    In the room, which had a shower, there were two beds and one window.Libellus I, Iter in Lūsitāniam

  • In cubiculō suō pater puerum, balneolō pluviō breviter lautum et linteō siccātum, veste nocturnā induit

    In their room Dad gave the boy a quick shower, dried him with a towel and put his pyjamas onLibellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium

  • forēs balneolī pluviī

    the shower doorTraupman 124

See also shower curtain, bathroom.

SourcesLewis & Short: balneum

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 124, checked against the searchable text of the book (29 October 2026).

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word.
